clue.text: Cash deposit-it can become very complicated

indicators.note: the letters of the cash deposit phrase are said to be able to turn into something else, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: A bank deposit, once made, can turn into a tangled business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can become' tells you to rearrange CASH DEPOSIT IT, thirteen letters, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intricate and elaborate in design is described as highly refined in this way.

clue.text: Sun's beginning to come over peninsula, a place often very cold

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece comes over, on top of, the next
the beginning of the word Sun's is its first letter

parts.note: Iberia is the peninsula holding Spain and Portugal

explanation.surface: Sunrise over the Spanish peninsula, contrasted with somewhere bitterly cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun's beginning' gives S, and 'to come over' puts it above IBERIA in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Siberia, the vast Russian region, is famous for its harsh, freezing winters.

clue.text: Teacher's cap doggie chewed

definitions.note: a possessive noun standing for an adjective meaning of or like a teacher

indicators.note: something a dog has chewed is mangled out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog has chewed the teacher's mortarboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chewed' signals an anagram of CAP DOGGIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedagogic means relating to teaching, so belonging to or typical of a teacher.

clue.text: Like metal that was first used in Greek tragedy

definitions.meaning: resembling or containing the metal iron

definitions.text: that was first used in Greek tragedy
definitions.meaning: dramatic ..., where the audience knows more than the characters, was a device of Greek tragedy

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses of one word: an adjective from iron, and the noun for saying or showing the opposite of the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means iron-like, and the noun names the dramatic device used by Sophocles.

clue.text: What Menuhin would initially do to acknowledge admirers

definitions.text: What Menuhin would initially do to acknowledge admirers

parts.words: What Menuhin would initially do to acknowledge admirers
parts.note: the violinist Yehudi Menuhin begins by picking up his bow before playing, and performers bend forward to thank applauding fans

explanation.walkthrough: Yehudi Menuhin was a celebrated violinist; the phrase means both picking up the violin bow and bowing to an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Performers acknowledge applause by bending forward, and a violinist starts by picking up his bow.

clue.text: Hint about item of hand luggage's capacity

indicators.note: the hint goes about, around, the item of luggage

parts.note: a cue is a hint or prompt
a bag is a piece of hand luggage

explanation.surface: A tip about how much a carry-on bag can hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the hint round the bag; the 's of luggage's stands for 'has', a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubage is cubic content, the volume or capacity of something.

clue.text: Number of people killed- American assassin found in roadside kiosk

parts.note: a death toll is the number killed
John Wilkes Booth assassinated President Lincoln

explanation.surface: A death toll, and Lincoln's killer turning up at a booth by the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' is a link: the pieces combine to make the kiosk.
explanation.definitionFit: A tollbooth is the small roadside cabin where drivers pay to use a road or bridge.

clue.text: Prevent grass coming up round end of plot

indicators.note: the reversed grass goes round the final letter of plot
in a down clue, coming up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

indicators.note: the end of plot is its last letter

explanation.surface: Stopping weeds from sprouting around the edge of a garden plot.
explanation.walkthrough: REED read upwards gives DEER, which goes round T, the end of 'plot'.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter is to discourage or prevent someone from acting.

clue.text: A little light used in each feature of church service

indicators.note: the little light is put in the word for each

parts.note: per means for each, as in a pound per head
a ray is a narrow beam of light

explanation.surface: Candles lit at every part of a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' signals a container: the little beam of light sits inside the word for each.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken prayers to God are a central element of a church service.

clue.text: Solid foundation — make this and young child may rest at night?

definitions.meaning: the solid rock beneath soil, figuratively the basic principles

definitions.text: make this and young child may rest at night?
definitions.meaning: if you rock the bed, a little child is soothed to sleep

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as the instruction 'bed, rock' for getting a child to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedrock is the underlying solid rock, and so any firm basis for something.

clue.text: Support someone escaping round back of Strangeways

indicators.note: the escaper goes round the final letter of Strangeways

parts.note: a bolter is one who runs away

indicators.note: the back of Strangeways is its final letter

explanation.surface: Helping a prisoner break out of Strangeways jail.
explanation.walkthrough: BOLTER goes around S. Strangeways is a well-known prison in Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolster is to prop up or reinforce, like a long pillow supporting someone.

clue.text: Game in which runner perhaps gets through

parts.note: a runner is a long narrow rug, so it is one example
by can mean through, by means of

explanation.surface: In a ball game, a runner manages to break through the defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' is not an athlete but a long strip of carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby is a ball sport played by two teams of fifteen or thirteen.

clue.text: Verbals from a right heartless bloke repeatedly nobbling bishop

indicators.note: nobbling means getting hold of, so the repeated letters take hold of the bishop
the group of letters is given twice in a row
losing its heart means the middle letter goes

parts.note: a guy is a bloke
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bloke without a heart keeps getting at a bishop in a war of words.
explanation.walkthrough: GUY without its heart is GY; ARGY twice gives ARGYARGY, and 'nobbling' takes B into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbals is British slang for a slanging match, and argy-bargy is a noisy quarrel.

clue.text: Gram's not wrong as a scientific unit

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are put in the wrong order, so rearrange them

parts.note: the possessive is read as the plain word with its S, grams

explanation.surface: A gram is unhappily insisting it is not wrong to be a unit of science.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' signals an anagram of GRAMS NOT; 'as' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The angstrom is a tiny unit of length, a ten-billionth of a metre, used for atoms.

clue.text: The old chap, one having a religious madness

parts.note: taken as written
a man is a chap
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An elderly man in the grip of religious mania.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' just links the pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek theo-, god, plus mania gives a delusion of religious kind, such as believing oneself divine.

clue.text: Associate of Vienna Circle providing drug

definitions.meaning: the philosopher Karl ... was linked with the Vienna Circle of logical positivists
slang for a capsule of amyl nitrite, inhaled as a stimulant

explanation.walkthrough: 'providing' is a link between two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Karl Popper, Vienna-born philosopher, shares his surname with the slang word for an inhaled stimulant.

clue.text: In old athletics arena see a star leap about

indicators.note: about means scattered around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A star athlete jumps around in an ancient arena, for all to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals an anagram of A STAR LEAP; 'In' and 'see' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A palaestra was the wrestling school or exercise ground of ancient Greece and Rome.

clue.text: Debauched character, but not one to let down employees

definitions.text: Debauched character, but not one to let down employees

parts.words: Debauched character, but not one to let down employees
parts.note: a hard-drinking Shakespearean knight, whose name read in parts suggests letting the workforce fall

explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's fat, dissolute knight; his name read as 'fall staff' suggests letting workers down, which the clue denies.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Falstaff is the drunken, roguish companion of Prince Hal in Shakespeare's history plays.

clue.text: Watch the heart

definitions.meaning: slang for a timepiece, from its ticking
slang for the organ that beats in the chest

explanation.walkthrough: Two slang senses of one word; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a clock or wristwatch and the human heart are slang named after their regular beat.

clue.text: Oak maybe not completely down? Criticise old saw

indicators.note: in this down clue the first piece sits above the second
the word loses its final letter so it is not complete

parts.note: an oak is an example of a tree
to pan is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: An oak only partly felled, and criticism of an old saying.
explanation.walkthrough: TREE cut short is TRE, followed by PAN. 'old saw' looks like an old saying, but it is a surgical saw.
explanation.definitionFit: A trepan was an early surgical saw for cutting holes in the skull.

clue.text: One who has not yet been man of the match

definitions.text: One who has not yet been man of the match

parts.words: One who has not yet been man of the match
parts.note: the match is a wedding, and its man is the groom, so this is someone yet to marry

explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests sport, but here it is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: An unmarried man has never been the groom at a wedding.

clue.text: Garment torn around end

indicators.note: the word for torn goes around the word for end

parts.note: rent means torn, ripped
an aim is an end, a goal

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing ripped round the hem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals a container. 'end' looks like a tip or finish, but here it is a purpose or goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old word for clothing, here standing for an item of dress.

clue.text: Class system probed by Left's Social Services secretary

indicators.note: the class system is entered, probed, by the next piece

parts.note: a caste is a hereditary class system

explanation.surface: Politics about a left-wing minister poking at the class system.
explanation.walkthrough: CASTE takes L inside. Barbara Castle was Labour's Secretary of State for Social Services in the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbara Castle held the post of Secretary of State for Social Services in Harold Wilson's government.

clue.text: Fellows losing head may have something boxed ring

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: men are fellows
sailors box the compass by reciting all its points in order

explanation.surface: Headless men with a box holding a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: MEN loses its head to give EN. 'may have' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring something is to surround it, which is to enclose or encircle it.

clue.text: Church faces a huge upheaval

parts.note: OS means outsize, a clothing size

explanation.surface: A church confronts an enormous upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faces' joins CH to the front of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaos is complete disorder, as after a great upheaval.

clue.text: Resin that is about to be used as sealant for space module

indicators.text: to be used as sealant for
indicators.note: a sealant closes round a gap, so the turned letters enclose the module
about means turned round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
the LEM was Apollo's lunar excursion module

explanation.surface: A resin used to seal a spacecraft module.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the abbreviation backwards to EI, and 'to be used as sealant for' wraps it round the Apollo landing craft.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is a fragrant tropical tree resin used in varnishes and ointments.

clue.text: Individual taken up, companion greatly honoured

definitions.text: Individual taken up, companion greatly honoured

indicators.note: in a down clue taken up means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: one is an individual
CH is a Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Someone raised up and greatly honoured as a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: ONE upwards is ENO, plus CH. The patriarch Enoch walked with God and was taken up to heaven without dying.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Enoch walked with God and was taken by Him, a man raised and honoured.

clue.text: In contact with a good person, securing benefit

indicators.note: the outer letters secure, hold, the benefit inside them

parts.note: ST, for saint, is a good person
a gain is a benefit

explanation.surface: Touching a saintly person in hopes of reward.
explanation.walkthrough: A and ST surround GAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaning against a wall means touching it, in physical contact with it.

clue.text: One given a commission after the Rising?

definitions.text: One given a commission after the Rising?

parts.words: One given a commission after the Rising?
parts.note: after the Resurrection, Jesus sent out his followers to teach all nations, the Great Commission

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' suggests an armed uprising, but it is Christ's Resurrection.
explanation.definitionFit: The Twelve were sent out by the risen Christ to preach, each a messenger.

clue.text: Latest responsibility of picture restorers

definitions.meaning: most up to date, using the newest technology
read literally, the condition of the artwork is what restorers look after

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase meaning cutting-edge is read literally as the condition of a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Up-to-the-minute technology is described by this phrase, and literally it is a painting's condition.
